clue.text: Article revealing memorial's details, received by paper after pressure?

definitions.text: Article revealing memorial's details, received by paper after pressure?

parts.words: Article revealing memorial's details, received by paper after pressure
parts.note: describes the copy made when paper laid over an engraved church memorial plate is pressed and rubbed with wax so the engraving shows through

explanation.surface: A newspaper item exposes the facts behind a monument, printed under pressure from someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a news story and 'paper' a newspaper, but the article is an object, a sheet of paper pressed over a memorial brass, a funerary plaque set into a church floor, and rubbed until its image appears.
explanation.definitionFit: An image taken from an engraved church plaque by rubbing wax over paper reproduces every detail of the memorial.

clue.text: Whisper from man supporting king in defeat

indicators.note: in a down entry the man sits underneath, holding up what comes before
the king's letter is set inside the word for defeat

parts.note: to defeat is to beat
R is short for rex, Latin for king
a man is a he

explanation.surface: A whispered word comes from a man propping up a king who has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' works because this is a down clue: HE goes below BREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe a word is to utter it very softly, as in not breathing a syllable of a secret.

clue.text: Discomfited party, bound by agreement lacking, latitude, upset

indicators.note: the party word is tied up inside the other piece, which wraps around it
in a down clue, upset turns the shortened word upside down so it reads bottom to top
the agreement word goes without the latitude letter

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A party-goer is left embarrassed after a deal falls through over a matter of latitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DEA, which is DEAL less L ('lacking latitude'), into AED in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone discomfited is embarrassed or disconcerted, the same feeling as being shamefaced.

clue.text: Naughty lady reset weighing apparatus

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters that refuse to stay in their order

explanation.surface: A badly behaved woman sets something back to zero on the scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reset' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'Naughty' rearranges LADY plus RESET.
explanation.definitionFit: A steelyard is an old balance with a long arm and sliding weight, used for weighing goods.

clue.text: Issue, new out, in colour

indicators.note: out says the letter for new is dropped from the word for issue

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a number

explanation.surface: A new edition comes out in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a brown earth pigment, and so the name of a shade.

clue.text: Cushion on edge of seat

parts.note: describes the padded raised side of a car or sofa seat that holds the sitter in place

explanation.surface: A soft pad sits at the rim of a chair, as if someone were on the edge of their seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on edge of seat' suggests excitement, but it is literal: the padded side wings of a sports car seat are its side pads.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolster is a long firm pillow, and seat makers use the word for the padded wings along a seat's sides.

clue.text: Story completely written up after half a month

indicators.note: half a means only the first four of the month's eight letters are used
in a down clue, written up means the word is set upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: completely, as in all over, gives all

explanation.surface: A tale is wholly drafted after the middle of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: NOVE is half of NOVEMBER; 'written up' turns ALL to LLA beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a story longer than a short story but shorter than a full book.

clue.text: Large rope, to enclose area of cricket field, initially required

indicators.note: the rope word wraps around the cricket area and the first letter

parts.note: a cable is a thick rope
the on side is the half of a cricket field on the batter's leg side

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A big rope is needed to fence off part of a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON SIDE is the half of a cricket field behind the batter's legs; it and R go between C and ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Considerable means sizeable or substantial, a synonym for large.

clue.text: Work from fool devoid of depth and merit

indicators.note: devoid of means the fool word goes without the depth letter

parts.note: a dope is a fool
to merit something is to rate it

explanation.surface: Some work comes from an idiot who lacks depth and worth.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Revered bishop, seen by returning delegate, very withdrawn

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: returning means the shortened word is read backwards
withdrawn means the letter for very is taken out of the delegate word

parts.note: to delegate a task is to devolve it

explanation.surface: A respected bishop is seen with an envoy who has gone home and become very reclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delegate' looks like a noun, a representative, but it is the verb DEVOLVE; it loses a V ('very withdrawn') to give DEVOLE, which 'returning' turns to ELOVED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beloved is dearly loved and cherished, as a revered figure is held in deep affection.

clue.text: Cleaner faced stint working around home

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters go about the word for home
working, as in being worked over, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: in, as in staying in, means at home

explanation.surface: A cleaner tackles a shift at home with a straight face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges FACED STINT into DISFECTANT, and 'around' puts IN (home) inside it after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A disinfectant is a chemical used to clean surfaces by killing germs.

clue.text: Bag a telephone to ring companion after end of revels

indicators.note: after puts the other pieces behind the letter from revels
end of takes the final letter of the word that follows
to ring means to surround, so the phone word encircles the companion

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone grabs a bag and a phone to call a friend once the party's over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests making a call but means encircle; CH is Companion of Honour, an order awarded by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A satchel is a shoulder bag, traditionally carried by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Baby's toys, right and left, in untidy state

indicators.note: the left letter is placed inside the jumbled word
untidy means the letters of state are messed up

explanation.surface: An infant's playthings are scattered all over the place, left and right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' scrambles STATE to ATTES, and 'in' puts L inside it to give ATTLES after R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattles are noisy shaking playthings given to infants.

clue.text: Terrible day to study

parts.note: to read a subject at university is to study it

explanation.surface: Having a day of studying sounds awful.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective dread means fearful or awe-inspiring, much as terrible once meant causing terror.

clue.text: Discover a spot outside church beside river

indicators.note: the spot word goes around the church and river letters

parts.note: a stain is a spot or mark

indicators.note: beside places the river letter next to the church letters

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone finds a mark on the wall of a church next to a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascertain is to find out for certain, a synonym of finding out.

clue.text: Entertainers in headphones wrapping one audition tape up

indicators.note: the headphones word wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: cans is slang for headphones

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the tape word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a demo is a sample recording sent to win an audition
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Performers wearing headphones bundle up a tape made for an audition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DEMO in this down clue; 'cans' is British slang for headphones.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedians are comic performers, a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Rubbish found by group covering road in city

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: covering means the group word goes over the road abbreviation

parts.note: a team is a group

explanation.surface: Litter is found by a crew resurfacing a street in town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: See star in unusual form in part of mosaic

indicators.note: unusual form says the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Look at a star picked out in an odd shape in a mosaic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square tiles that make up a mosaic.

clue.text: Letter ending in garbage on street in heap

indicators.note: ending in takes the final letter of the word that follows
the street abbreviation is set inside the heap word

parts.note: a pile is a heap

explanation.surface: A letter ends up in the rubbish heaped on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: An epistle is a formal letter, as in the epistles of the New Testament.

clue.text: Decline drinks vocally

indicators.note: vocally means the word is spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a cat laps milk, so laps means drinks

explanation.surface: Someone turns down drinks out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refusing, but it is falling off, and 'drinks' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a falling-off or decline, as in a lapse in standards.

clue.text: Drink described as alcoholic in false statement?

indicators.note: the alcoholic drink is placed inside the word for a false statement

parts.note: a lie is a false statement
mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey

explanation.surface: A soft drink is passed off as alcoholic in a fib.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alcoholic' stands for an alcoholic drink, MEAD, which sits inside LIE; the soft drink is what the lie disguises.
explanation.definitionFit: Limeade is a soft drink made from lime juice, sugar and water.

clue.text: Keep going forward, skirting southern islands

indicators.note: skirting means the forward word goes round the other letters

parts.note: forward, as in cheeky, means pert

explanation.surface: Push on ahead, going round the islands to the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' suggests direction but is the adjective meaning cheeky, PERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to carry on despite difficulty, a synonym of continuing.

clue.text: Top vehicle at front of rank

indicators.note: at front of places the vehicle word before the rank word

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
a tier is a rank or row

explanation.surface: The best vehicle leads the queue at the taxi rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like best but is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a close-fitting strapless top worn by women.

clue.text: Show again cherished by admirer uncritically

indicators.note: cherished, as in held close, signals that the answer is held inside these words

explanation.surface: A fan uncritically loves to watch a programme again.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a programme is to broadcast it a second time.

clue.text: Broadcast item read without a fault

indicators.note: broadcast, as in scattered like seed, means the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: An item is read on air without any mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ITEM READ, with an A taken out ('without a'), rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A demerit is a mark against someone for a fault or offence.

clue.text: Prince with function revolving around European court

indicators.note: around means the reversed word goes about the other letters
revolving means the function word is turned round

parts.note: a role is a function

explanation.surface: A prince takes on a part touring a European court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns the function word round to ELOR; the Prince is one of the German Electors of the Holy Roman Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: The Electors were the German princes entitled to choose the Holy Roman Emperor.

clue.text: Number led by sailor in song referring to peninsula

indicators.note: led by puts the other pieces in front of the number letter
the sailor abbreviation sits inside the song word

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
AB is an able-bodied seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A number is led off by a sailor singing a song about a peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabian describes things of Arabia, the large peninsula in western Asia.

clue.text: To stay out of debt, gather tips?

definitions.meaning: to manage on what one earns without borrowing
read literally, bring the ends of things together so they touch

explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' suggests money, which fits the debt theme, but it means ends brought together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having just enough income to cover costs; read literally it means bringing two ends together.
